summary: This component checks if a blog post is older than one year and displays an appropriate warning to readers. If the post has a recent review date, it shows a green success notice saying the content is still accurate; otherwise, it shows a yellow warning that the information may be outdated. If the post is less than a year old, it renders nothing.

explanations.28: useBlogPost() is a Docusaurus hook that gives us access to the current blog post's data, including its metadata (which contains the publish date and other fields).
explanations.33: We're casting these fields to TypeScript types because they're custom fields this blog added to the standard metadata — Docusaurus doesn't know about them by default, so we have to tell TypeScript what shape they have.
explanations.39: We sort the updates array in reverse chronological order (newest first) by converting the date strings to timestamps and comparing them.
explanations.46: We create a new Date object representing right now, so we can compare it against the post date.
explanations.47: We subtract one year from today's date, so now oneYearAgo represents the cutoff point — anything before this date is considered old.
explanations.57: We check if the review date is recent enough (at or after the one-year-ago threshold) to override the old post warning.
explanations.60: toLocaleDateString formats the date into a readable string like 'January 15, 2024' using US English formatting.
explanations.68: clsx() is a utility that combines multiple CSS class names together, letting us apply both Docusaurus's built-in alert styles and our custom styles at the same time.
explanations.72: aria-hidden='true' tells screen readers to ignore the emoji, so they don't read out random characters — the text message itself conveys the meaning to everyone.
